messages.content: Predict one person’s actual contribution in a repeated collective-loss task. Six real people remain in the same anonymous group for 10 periods, interacting in real time. They are identified by stable displayed numbers 1–6: members 1–3 are in one city and 4–6 in another. The exact other city is not disclosed. Country information is supplied only if it was announced in this person’s condition; never infer the other city’s country from hidden researcher treatment labels. This is a NO-SANCTIONS condition. In every period each person receives 60 tokens and simultaneously chooses an integer number of tokens from 0 through 50 to put into the collective fund. Keep the rest, 60 minus the contribution, in the private account; at least 10 tokens therefore remain private each period. Contributions are not transfers to one particular group member. There is no sanction choice or sanction cost in this condition. The current choices of the other five people have not been revealed when the person chooses. After a completed contribution period, feedback includes every numbered member’s contributions in all previous periods and the probability of avoiding a collective loss determined by cumulative group contributions. The whole group’s contributions across all 10 periods count towards a fixed safety threshold of 2100 tokens. At the end of period 10 let G be this group total, and let A=600 minus this person’s total contributions be their accumulated private tokens. Loss is avoided with probability P=min(G/2100,1), the same for everyone. If loss is avoided, the person keeps A; otherwise 75% of A is lost and they keep A/4. Thus G=0 implies certain loss and G at least 2100 implies certain safety. There is one terminal loss event, not a fresh loss imposed in every period. Token exchange into the person’s local currency is specified below. Original instructions about any extra participation fee, practice, payment rounding and exact screen layout are not locally available; do not invent them or pretend to quote the original task framing. All known earlier group contributions in this ten-period game are retained. Reported probabilities and balances before the current choice are derived from those earlier actions and the announced rules, not assumed to be the exact decimal precision of the original screen. Current group contributions, future periods, final probability, realized loss and final earnings are not inputs. Personal background items were linked from recruitment and the post-interaction questionnaire: only concrete self information reasonably stable during the session is supplied. Collection after play does not make later attitudes, trust/risk or Schwartz scores prior traits. Literal place/language/study descriptions are original-language responses, with only recorded reversible character-encoding repairs; spelling and scope errors are not replaced by inferred citizenship, education or psychology. Missing items are not imputed. Small reported childhood populations are kept as literal reports, not silently multiplied by a thousand. Output only the chosen integer token amount, 0–50, without explanation.
